ITI Student Handbook
Welcome to the
Information
Technology Institute
Today, you join a legacy built by thousands of exceptional minds. These
are individuals who stepped through our doors with a raw passion for
technology and left as industry pioneers, global innovators, and leaders
shaping digital landscapes. Today, that story becomes your story.
The path ahead will demand your absolute focus, your curiosity, and
your determination. You will be pushed to think deeply, experiment
boldly, and build solutions that don't just solve code, but elevate
communities and transform the lives of millions.
Now, the torch is passed to you. Challenge your thinking. Push your
capabilities. Bring your unique passion and your resilience to the table
every single day.
We vow to make your time here a transformative launchpad for a
brilliant career. Work hard, dream big, and always remember—ITI will be
your home, long after you graduate.
Welcome on board. Let's leave an impact together.
Best Wishes,
Dr. Heba Saleh, ITI Chairwoman

ITI Student Handbook
ITI TRAINING PROGRAMS
OVERVIEW
PROFESSIONAL TRAINING PROGRAM
A full-time, 9-Month government-funded scholarship program designed to
prepare talented Egyptian university graduates for high-demand jobs in
Egypt and abroad.
KEY FEATURES:
Starts every October
Over 30 specialized tracks tailored to ICT market needs
Strong partnerships with industry leaders
Employment rate over 85%
Only 10% of applicants are accepted after a rigorous selection process
ELIGIBILITY:
Egyptian nationals with a Bachelor’s degree
Graduated within the last 5 academic years
Full-time commitment required
Male applicants must have completed, postponed, or been exempted
from military service
INTENSIVE CODE CAMP (ICC)
A shorter, highly-focused training program offering tracks that match market
demands in tech and digital industries.
KEY FEATURES:
Runs twice every year.
4~6 Months, full-time immersive training format
Over 40 specialized tracks tailored to ICT market needs
Strong focus on market-relevant technologies
ELIGIBILITY:
Egyptian graduates with a Bachelor’s degree
Graduated within the last 10 academic years
Full-time commitment required
Male applicants must have completed, postponed, or been exempted
from military service

ITI Student Handbook
CODE OF CONDUCT & DRESS CODE
All students are expected to maintain a respectful, responsible, and professional
demeanor at all times. The following principles apply to both online and onsite
settings:
CONDUCT PRINCIPLES
Show respect for instructors, staff, fellow students, and all ITI personnel.
Maintain the integrity of facilities, equipment, and shared learning
environments.
Participate actively in lectures, discussions, and team activities.
Follow ITI policies regarding academic honesty and constructive
feedback.
The institute maintains a zero-tolerance policy for misbehavior and
abusive or offensive language.
Disciplinary action may be taken for any behavior that disrupts the
learning environment or tarnishes our values.
DRESS CODE
Students must present themselves in a manner appropriate for a professional
training environment. This applies during both in-person attendance and
online sessions:
Wear clean, modest, and tidy attire at all times.
Closed-toed shoes are mandatory onsite.
Avoid shorts, ripped jeans, slippers, flip-flops, or beachwear.
Skirts must be at or below the knee.
Hair should be neat and grooming should align with Egyptian workplace
norms.
Face coverings (such as niqabs, masks, or caps) must be removed during
exams, assessments, or identification processes for security purposes.
Note: If a student’s attire is deemed inappropriate, Student Affairs reserves
the right to issue a verbal or written warning and require a change of
dress.

PROHIBITIONS
The following actions are strictly forbidden and may result in immediate
disciplinary procedures:
Smoking anywhere on campus (including restrooms and open spaces).
Eating or drinking inside computer labs, classrooms, or near electronic
equipment.
Using mobile phones during lectures or exams without permission.
Engaging in political, religious, or commercial activities on ITI premises.
Upholding the ITI code of conduct contributes to a safe, inclusive, and
effective learning environment for all.

ITI Student Handbook
ASSESSMENT & GRADING
Understanding how your performance is assessed is the key to your success at ITI.
This section outlines how assignments, exams, and overall progress are evaluated
throughout the program.
COURSE OUTLINE Your course syllabus, which explains learning goals, how
you’ll be graded, and all key deadlines, will be available
online.
ASSIGNMENTS All assignments must follow provided instructions. Late
submissions are penalized with a 5-point deduction per
day unless an extension is granted in advance.
EXAMS A minimum of 60% is required to pass any course.
Some tracks may use cumulative assessments. Late
arrival up to 20% of exam time is allowed with penalty;
more than that, the student loses the right to take the
exam. One corrective exam may be granted at the
discretion of the Academic Supervisor.
CORRECTIVE EXAMS Only one opportunity is granted for a corrective exam
per subject, subject to Academic Affairs approval.
Failing the corrective exam results in course failure.
PROGRESS REVIEW Students who fail two courses during the program will
be dismissed. Continued poor performance or failure
to meet project milestones may trigger additional
academic review.
ACADEMIC INTEGRITY Students must submit their own work and cite all
sources. Plagiarism or cheating leads to a score of zero,
exam dismissal, and possible disciplinary action. Misuse
of AI, sharing answers, or unapproved collaboration is
also prohibited. When in doubt, ask your instructor.

ITI Student Handbook
SUPPORT SERVICES & FACILITIES
To support your learning and productivity, ITI provides a range of digital tools, lab
resources, and technical assistance to ensure a smooth training experience.
COMPUTER LABS &
EQUIPMENT
Labs are equipped with licensed
software and antivirus protection.
Students must keep workstations
clean. Equipment may be
borrowed when available and
should be reported immediately if
damaged.
LIBRARY ACCESS
Offers both digital and printed
resources. A valid student ID is
required for entry.
TECHNICAL SUPPORT
TSU assists with any technical
problems involving ITI equipment
or platforms. Prompt reporting is
encouraged. Room 3014.
VOICE-OUT UNIT
The Voice-Out Unit offers students a safe, neutral channel to share personal or academic
concerns. Whether related to course content, instructor behavior, or general well-being,
students can submit concerns confidentially and expect a structured response. The unit
operates independently from academic assessment and works closely with Student
Affairs to ensure fairness, confidentiality, and resolution. Room 3016.

16
ITI Student Handbook
TRANSCRIPTS &
RECORDS
Each graduate receives one official transcript upon program completion. Additional copies
are available upon request for a fee.
All transcript requests must be made in person or via official email to the Student Affairs
Office. Requests by phone or fax are not accepted.
Transcripts issued to third parties (such as employers or embassies) require a signed
authorization letter from the student.
Processing time for transcripts may take up to five working days.
ITI does not issue unofficial transcripts or academic records through informal channels.
